nodes.name: Fe-NiO hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam (NF, 4 cm × 3 cm) was pretreated by 3 M HCl under sonication and washed by deionized water and alcohol three times, respectively. 2.33 g Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.15 g NH₄F, 1.20 g CO(NH₂)₂ and 0.06 g Fe(C₅H₇O₂)₃ were added to 70 mL of deionized water and stirred for 10 min to mix well. Then, the solution was transferred to a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave containing treated NF and heated at 120 °C for 6 h. After removing the impurity with anhydrous ethanol and drying overnight in a vacuum at 60 °C, the precursor was calcined in air at 350 °C for 2 h (5 °C/min) to obtain Fe-NiO.

nodes.name: NiO hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam (NF, 4 cm × 3 cm) was pretreated by 3 M HCl under sonication and washed by deionized water and alcohol three times, respectively. 2.33 g Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.15 g NH₄F, 1.20 g CO(NH₂)₂ (without Fe(C₅H₇O₂)₃) were added to 70 mL of deionized water and stirred for 10 min to mix well. Then, the solution was transferred to a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave containing treated NF and heated at 120 °C for 6 h. After removing the impurity with anhydrous ethanol and drying overnight in a vacuum at 60 °C, the precursor was calcined in air at 350 °C for 2 h (5 °C/min) to obtain NiO.

nodes.name: Ni₂P phosphating
nodes.procedure: Ni₂P was obtained by phosphating NiO, and the mass ratio of NiO to NaH₂PO₂ was 1:3. NiO and NaH₂PO₂ were placed in two porcelain boats and calcined at 350 °C in N₂ atmosphere for 2 h, with a heating rate of 5 °C/min.
nodes.source_text: Ni₂P was obtained by phosphating NiO, and the mass ratio of NiO to NaH₂PO₂ was 1:3.

nodes.name: NiO/Ni₂P phosphating
nodes.procedure: NiO/Ni₂P were synthesized as the same method of Fe-NiO/Ni₂P, without adding Fe(C₅H₇O₂)₃. NiO was first prepared by hydrothermal method without Fe precursor, then phosphated with NaH₂PO₂ (mass ratio 1:1.5) at 350 °C in N₂ atmosphere for 2 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-NiO/Ni2P shows lattice spacing of 0.222 nm (111) plane of Ni₂P and 0.219 nm (400) plane of NiO; both increased after Fe doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Fe-NiO/Ni₂P, the lattice spacing of 0.222 nm corresponded to the (111) plane of Ni₂P, and the lattice spacing of 0.219 nm was assigned to the (400) plane of NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-NiO/Ni2P contains Fe, Ni, O, and P elements with Fe evenly distributed and P/O in outer/inner regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) areal scan displays that Fe-NiO/Ni₂P contained Fe, Ni, O and P elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-NiO/Ni2P shows characteristic peaks of NiO (222, 400, 440 planes) and Ni₂P (111, 210, 300 planes) with negative shift due to Fe doping-induced lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The three diffraction peaks at 37.3°, 43.3° and 62.9° were indexed to the (222), (400), and (440) crystal planes of NiO... Both Fe-NiO/Ni₂P and NiO/Ni₂P corresponded well to the characteristic peaks of NiO and Ni₂P.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-NiO/Ni₂P contains Fe, Ni, O, P; Fe 2p: 711.5/723.7 eV (oxidized Fe, Fe-O), 707.4/717.6 eV (Fe-P confirming O-Fe-P bond); Ni 2p peaks at 857.0/875.0 eV (Ni²⁺), 860.5/879.0 eV (Ni³⁺) shifted to higher binding energy; O 1s blue shifted at 531.3 eV (M-O); P 2p shifted lower at 134.1 eV (P-O), 129.2 eV (P-M).
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the survey spectra, Fe-NiO/Ni₂P contained Fe, Ni, O and P... The peaks at 711.5 and 723.7 eV in the Fe 2p spectrum corresponded to oxidized Fe... The peaks at 707.4 and 717.6 eV were attributed to the Fe-P bond.
